principle: Namespace qualification that the enclosing scope already supplies — a prefix on a name, or an `open` of a namespace already open — is not repeated.
A `Decidable` instance is implemented by a computation of the lowest available complexity rather than by transcribing the proposition's definition.
A lemma that rewrites an expression to a strictly simpler normal form is tagged `@[simp]`.
When the core of a proof or construction is a fact about a more general object, it is stated on its own at that general level and the specific result is derived from it.

A goal that a standard finishing tactic (`simp`, `rfl`, `ring`, `module`, `grind`, `grw`, `aesop`, `trivial`, `fun_prop`) closes is closed by that tactic, not by a hand-assembled term or rewrite chain.
A one-argument lambda that only passes its argument to a function is written with the `·` placeholder rather than a named binder.
Declarations added to a file use the variables the file already declares rather than introducing duplicate copies of them.
A notion the library already defines (a predicate, a combinator, a structure) is used by name rather than re-encoded ad hoc in the statement or definition.
A new definition or instance comes with the lemmas that rewrite its applications (`_apply`, `coe_`), so downstream proofs never unfold it.
A structure or class instance is written with `where` syntax rather than an anonymous constructor, record braces or a tactic-mode `constructor`.
A definition or theorem stated for a special case is generalised to the parameter it depends on when the special case is recovered by instantiation.
A result the existing library already provides (possibly after exhibiting the object as an instance of the relevant structure) is derived from that API rather than proved again from first principles.
Consecutive top-level commands (`namespace`, `variable`, declarations) are separated by exactly one blank line, never two.
A local `have` or `let` with a short body and few uses is inlined at its use rather than bound to a name.
A terminal `simp`, `simpa` or `simp_all` call uses the default simp set with extra lemmas as needed rather than `simp only` with an explicit list.
A structure that extends another is defined directly with all its fields, not in two stages through a named instance of the parent structure.
A `simp` or `grind` call does not list lemmas that are already in the tactic's default set or that it does not need.

An annotation that elaboration supplies on its own — an explicit coercion function, a type ascription, an argument that can be inferred or left to `..`, a structure field that its auto-param discharges — is not written out.

Consecutive steps that a single construct can perform (two `simp`s, a `rw` then a `simp`, a `specialize` then a `convert`, a `let .some … | …` followed by a `match` on its result) are merged into one call.
A declaration's name is built from the constants that actually appear in its statement, following the naming convention.
An instance-implicit argument is left unnamed and recovered with `‹_›` or by inference rather than bound to a name.
A construction that could conflict with a non-definitionally-equal instance on the same type is declared as a `def`, not an `instance`.
A collection of lemmas repeatedly supplied to `simp` locally is registered as a named simp set or tagged `@[simp]` rather than listed with `attribute [local simp]` or in each call.
A lemma whose dual (opposite category, left/right, additive/multiplicative) holds is stated together with that dual.
A non-terminal `simp` is squeezed to `simp only` only when the following tactic depends on the exact goal shape; before a flexible tactic it is left as is.
An automation call (`grind`, `aesop`, `simp`) replaces an explicit proof only when it is not slower and no short readable explicit proof exists.
A module docstring's title and summary name precisely what the file contains, not a broader topic it might suggest.
A definition is an `abbrev` only when it must be reducible for typeclass inference or definitional unfolding; otherwise it is a `def`.
A docstring describes exactly the statement it documents, with the same hypotheses and objects, not a simplified paraphrase or a bare title.
A commonly needed variant or special case of a lemma is stated as its own lemma alongside it.
A docstring is a standalone explanation of its declaration, not a contrast with another declaration.
An import, `open`, `variable`, `section` or section modifier (`noncomputable section`) that another already provides, or that nothing in the file uses or needs, is removed.
A field or projection is named after the library's established name for the same role in analogous structures (`fst`/`snd` for product projections, `inl`/`inr` for coproduct injections).
A multi-line declaration header breaks between the binders and the statement, keeping the conclusion on one line where it fits, rather than splitting it mid-expression.
A constant whose namespace the expected type determines is written with leading-dot notation rather than fully qualified.
Two lemmas each giving half of a conclusion are replaced by one lemma with the combined stronger conclusion.
A lemma about a literal constant (`0`, `1`, `⊤`) whose carrier type cannot be inferred from other arguments takes the type as an explicit argument.
A declaration in a namespace whose short name would shadow a commonly used root-level name (`zero`, `one`, `map`) is marked `protected`.
A reusable step performed inline in a proof or construction (a conversion between two forms of a definition, an auxiliary map) is extracted as its own API lemma or definition.
A PR created with AI assistance follows the AI contribution guidelines: it discloses that fact and the manner of use in its description.
A proof is kept as short as a reasonable reader can make it; a visibly compressible proof is golfed.
A change to a tool's observable output (message severity, format) is checked for downstream tooling that depends on it.
A proof that is a single lemma application or anonymous constructor with short arguments is written as one term rather than as a tactic block with `apply`/`constructor` and bullets.
A PR introducing a new concept, a non-obvious design choice or a change whose benefit is not self-evident explains its motivation and intended use in the description or module docstring.
A tactic's argument syntax reuses an existing syntax category (binders, `intro`/`rintro` patterns) rather than introducing a new parser for the same notion.

A PR is kept to one coherent unit; parts that can be reviewed separately (a file move, a preliminary refactor) or that need separate design discussion or further development are split into their own PRs.
A docstring, module or declaration, ends with `-/` immediately after its last line of text, not on a line of its own and with no blank line before it.
A lemma assumes a hypothesis, or ambient data such as a valuation, only when the statement needs it; an unnecessary assumption is dropped and a stronger-than-needed one is weakened to what is used.
A module docstring's list of main definitions and results covers all of them; when a PR adds results to a file, the docstring is updated to mention them.
An argument that appears only in the conclusion and in no hypothesis is explicit.
A `match` on an inductive type names every constructor it passes through unchanged rather than using a wildcard catch-all.
Anonymous functions are written with `↦`, not `=>`.
Arguments common to several consecutive declarations are declared once with `variable` rather than repeated in each signature.
A result whose converse also holds is stated as an iff.
A new file is imported in `Mathlib.lean` so that CI builds it.
A new file is a `module` with its content in an `@[expose] public section` unless a smaller public API is deliberately curated.
Plain `intro` is used when it handles the patterns; `rintro` is reserved for patterns `intro` cannot destructure.
In a mechanical cleanup, a hunk that makes the code longer or less readable is left out rather than applied for uniformity.
A term that already has the required type is supplied directly, not wrapped in a tactic block that merely produces it (`by exact e`, `by simpa using e`, `by infer_instance` for `inferInstance`).
Grouping delimiters the parser does not need — extra parentheses, braces around a tactic block, `<|` before a trailing `fun` — are omitted.
An instance that typeclass inference already finds is removed rather than redeclared (kept as an `example` at most).
A file-wide `set_option` (such as a linter threshold) is placed where the library's other files place the same option.
A function or lemma in the namespace of its argument's type is applied with dot notation (`x.f`, `h.foo`) rather than `T.f x`.

Spacing follows the style guide: a single space between tokens — after each comma, around infix operators and `:=`, between a name and its binders, after `←` in a rewrite list, after a heading marker in a docstring — a space inside structure-instance braces, and none before a comma, after a prefix operator or inside brackets.
The dedicated library lemma is used rather than an equivalent composite assembled from other lemmas.
A class or structure is given an alternative constructor that, under a common extra assumption, asks only for the fields that do not follow from it.
A `refine` whose term contains no placeholder, or an `apply` that leaves no goals, is written as `exact`.
A statement is written beta-reduced; an applied lambda `(fun x ↦ e) a` is replaced by its value.

A chain of compositions or transitivity steps (`Eq.trans`, `refine … ?_`) whose intermediate terms are implicit or recorded in comments is written as a `calc` or `trans` chain that states them in code.
A message that proposes replacement syntax follows the standard `Try this:` format.
A recurring combination of hypotheses about an object is bundled into a Prop-valued class or structure that lemmas assume, rather than passing the data and hypotheses each time.
A declaration's statement continued onto a new line is indented by four spaces.
The components of a name follow the statement's structure: the head symbol of the left-hand side first, then its arguments in order, with projections and coercions (`coe_`, `toFoo_`) leading.
A lemma connecting two notions lives in the file of the more derived notion, so the more basic file does not import the more specialised one.
A declaration or file that is removed is given a deprecation alias or a redirecting stub, never silently deleted.
When a lemma name mentions another declaration, that declaration's name keeps its own camelCase spelling rather than being split into snake_case.
A deprecation whose replacement is not a drop-in substitute states in its message how to recover the old form.
Material whose topic or import requirements differ from a file's subject is placed in a new file, or in the existing file on its topic, rather than appended to that file.

A `set_option`, `omit`, `variable` binder change or typeclass assumption needed by only a few declarations is scoped to them — with `in`, or written in their own signatures — rather than applied to the rest of the file or section.

A workaround — a backward-compatibility option, an instance removed with `attribute [-instance]`, an adaptation note's substitute proof — is re-checked against current master and removed once no longer necessary.
A proof does not chain normalising tactics (`simp`, `norm_num`, `ring_nf`) whose interaction produces a large fragile goal; it rewrites into a clean form and finishes with one call.
A hypothesis whose necessity is not evident is justified in the docstring or a comment, or by a reference.
An unreachable case is closed with an explicit contradiction (`False.elim`, `absurd`) rather than a tactic that closes the goal as a side effect.
The test suite of an additive (or otherwise dualised) tool mirrors every test of the original that has an analogue.
When an attribute or convention is applied systematically, the deliberate exceptions are documented in a comment.
A deprecated declaration is kept only as an alias or a one-line derivation from its replacement, not with its original proof.
The simp lemmas about one function, and the analogues of a lemma across the library, all orient towards the same normal form; a lemma is not oriented against its siblings.
Lines respect the 100-character limit: code or prose that fits within it is kept on one line rather than wrapped early, and a line that exceeds it is broken.
A refactoring (of meta-code, of a class hierarchy or its instance priorities) preserves the existing behaviour in every case, including corner cases that do not currently arise.
A lemma that combines two independent operations is decomposed into a lemma for each operation, from which the combination follows.
A definition producing data is written as a term (pattern matching, direct construction), not built in tactic mode.
A PR whose content is unrelated to Mathlib (personal files, a test of scripts or automation) is closed; the repository is not a scratch space.
Meta-code that matches an expression against a known head constant uses `match_expr` or a Qq pattern rather than raw `mkApp`/`.const` constructor patterns.
An inequality step that follows by monotonicity or congruence is discharged by `gcongr` rather than by naming the specific monotonicity lemmas.

A lemma whose main hypothesis is a predicate `P x` takes that hypothesis as an explicit argument and is named in `P`'s namespace, so it is applied with dot notation, rather than being stated as an iff or in another namespace.
A safety check in meta-code is not bypassed by a flag for a special caller; the caller's context is adjusted (an instance locally removed) so that the check still runs.

A continuation block (tactic block, match-arm body, structure-instance fields, the continuation line of a bullet item in prose) is indented two spaces relative to its parent line, not further and not aligned to a delimiter.
Each tactic stands on its own line; several tactics are not joined with `;` on one line.
A PR that generalises or moves an existing declaration keeps its attributes (`@[simp]` and others) unchanged; an attribute change is made deliberately and separately.

An attribute on a declaration is placed on its own line above the declaration keyword rather than inline before it; required when the statement spans several lines, preferred even for a one-line declaration.
Commented-out code, leftover scaffolding comments and TODOs already carried out are removed before merging.
An instance obtained by inference after unfolding is supplied as `inferInstanceAs` with the unfolded type, not by `change`/`dsimp` followed by `infer_instance` in tactic mode.
A lemma stated as an equality of bundled maps (a composition equal to another map) is accompanied by its pointwise version applied to an element.
A new definition ships with the basic API lemmas that motivate it (closure under the standard operations, characterisations), not only the definition.
Two bundled maps that agree are related by an equation between the maps themselves, through the appropriate projection and tagged `@[simp]`, rather than only by a pointwise equation.

A variable is not named with a letter that carries an established meaning in the file's area (`ε` for a small real in analysis, `I` for an ideal) or that is easily confused with another symbol (`O` with `0`); the library's conventional letters (`R`, `S` in `Algebra R S`) are used.
An equality lemma is stated in one orientation only; the reverse is obtained with `.symm` rather than stated as a second lemma.

A definition or proof that follows a source (a textbook, the Stacks project, a paper) cites that source, in its docstring or with the `@[stacks]` attribute, so the convention adopted or the argument's origin is clear.
Side goals of a lemma application are supplied explicitly in a `refine` term rather than dispatched by `any_goals`/`try`/`<;>` combinator chains.
A new type or definition for a notion the library already names in another guise takes the established name rather than a fresh one.
A definition's docstring is a noun phrase naming the object defined, not a sentence describing what the function does.
Nested single-binder lambdas `fun a ↦ fun b ↦ e` are written as one lambda with several binders `fun a b ↦ e`.
A lemma or auxiliary definition that exposes the implementation of a definition and serves only to build its public API is marked `private`.
A definition, notation or instance is not introduced only to be unfolded by a `@[simp]` lemma; either it is the simp normal form or it is not added.

When the data at hand fits a structure's constructor, the structure is built directly from it rather than through an intermediate object and a conversion, and the intermediate is dropped if nothing else needs it.
A predicate or function on values of a type `T` is declared in `T`'s namespace so that it is written with dot notation (`s.IsDiscrete`).
A lemma whose formal statement obscures its meaning (filter language, an encoding) carries a docstring stating it in plain words.
A line break inside a declaration or expression comes after a connective token (`:`, `→`, `∧`, `=`), not before it.
A step that contributes nothing (an unused `have`, a rewrite the closing step already covers, a check that a later call repeats) is removed.
A lemma that another lemma duplicates or that a general API lemma subsumes is deprecated in favour of that lemma rather than kept, or pointed at, alongside it.
A structure or subtype element used as a function or as an element of its carrier is written through its coercion (`x v`, `↑x`), not through the raw projection (`x.1 v`, `x.val v`, `x.toLinear`).
A lemma that replaces one notion by another, rather than simplifying within one, is tagged `@[simp]` only when the target notion is the agreed normal form.
A structure of morphisms or data determined by its fields carries `@[ext]` globally, not only as a local attribute.
A non-obvious arrangement in a file (an unusual import, a deliberate omission) or a non-obvious choice within a proof or a definition's body is explained by a comment at the place it is made.
A docstring is written in complete sentences, beginning with a capital letter and each ending with a full stop.
Within a PR or a file, the same kind of step or the same notation is written the same way throughout (`have` or `haveI`, one spelling, one spacing), not in mixed forms.
A definition states its type explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred from the body.
A simp lemma whose right-hand side is a `match` or `if` is replaced by one simp lemma per case, each with a concrete argument.
A monotonicity lemma concluding `f a ≤ f b` from `a ≤ b` is named `f_le_f`, without an `_of_le` suffix for the evident hypothesis.
A long proof or construction inside a definition or instance is split off into a (private) auxiliary lemma or definition rather than written inline, even if used once.
A reference to the literature names the work and points to the precise location in it (chapter, section, tag); a vague mention of unnamed sources is dropped or made specific.
A fix or improvement made to one of a family of analogous tools or declarations is applied to its siblings as well.
A `simp` that feeds another tactic is not hidden inside `simpa using by tac`; it is written as a visible `simp only [...]` followed by that tactic, or folded into the tactic's own lemma list.
A `conv` targets its subterm by pattern (`conv in`) rather than by a navigation path (`lhs; rhs; enter`).
A module docstring uses only the section headings the style guide prescribes; ad hoc headings are removed and their text merged into the prose.
The `Authors:` line of a file's header, and a PR's co-author credits, list every contributor.
A property that the PR's title or docstring ascribes to an object in the library's own terms (`Splits`, `IsCompact`) is stated as a lemma in that term, not left implicit in an equivalent formulation.
Within a statement or term-mode body spanning several lines, each line continuing a subexpression is indented two spaces beyond the line it continues, so indentation mirrors nesting.
A change of marginal benefit (cosmetic spacing in prose, minor docstring polish) is not made when reviewing it costs more than it gains.
A new or changed piece of meta-code (tactic, attribute, command, syntax) comes with tests in the test suite that exercise it.
A declaration's name is cased by its kind: a structure, inductive or `Type`/`Prop`-valued definition in UpperCamelCase, a function or term in lowerCamelCase, a theorem in snake_case.
An implicit argument that must be pinned is supplied directly (`@f a`, `(x := a)`, an explicit-argument variant `mk'`) rather than through a type ascription of the whole term.
A definition's docstring accounts for every component of its type — each non-obvious argument and each part of the result — not only the headline one.
A lemma concluding `f a ≤ f b` (or `<`) from `a ≤ b`, possibly with side conditions, is tagged `@[gcongr]`.
A term containing `?_` placeholders is passed to `refine`, not `apply`.
A comment or docstring describing code matches that code (its names and its steps); when the code changes, it is updated in the same change so that it stays accurate.
An automation call (`aesop`, `simp`, `grind`) is not replaced by explicit lemma names unless a benchmark shows it slow; such a change states its measured motivation.
A file all of whose declarations are deprecated is itself marked as a deprecated module.
When a definition has a preferred lemma for unfolding or using it, the definition's docstring points to that lemma.

Variables introduced by `induction` or `cases` are named through the structured `with | case x ih =>` syntax, not through the primed `induction'`/`cases'` forms, a `refine` of the recursor with `?_` goals and `intro`s, or recovered afterwards with `rename_i`.
A lemma whose conclusion is a predicate `P x` is named `P.of_<hypothesis>` in `P`'s namespace, so that it is written `.of_h h` against the expected type.
A variant of an existing lemma is distinguished by a suffix naming what differs (`_of_<hypothesis>`), not by a prime.

A `by_cases` one of whose branches is impossible under the hypotheses, or whose branches do not use the case hypothesis, is replaced by the direct proof (a `have` of the fact that holds, or the one-arm proof).
A hypothesis that is a conjunction or existential whose components are always used separately is destructured when introduced (`obtain ⟨_, _⟩`), not projected with `.1`/`.2` at each use.
A definition's name, notation or a docstring's wording uses the standard mathematical term or convention for the notion, not one whose established meaning differs or a non-standard one.
A statement or use site does not need `@`, placeholder underscores or a type ascription to elaborate; a name or API that forces them is changed so that ordinary application suffices.
An `iff` lemma whose directions are useful on their own is accompanied by `alias ⟨_, _⟩` names for each direction, so each can be used with dot notation.
A lemma that is a direct instance of an existing general lemma, provable by applying it with no further work, is not added; the general lemma is used.
A lemma or instance states the strongest conclusion its proof gives (the tightest bound, the stronger filter, `Unique` over `Subsingleton`), not a weaker consequence of it.
A PR's title and description say concretely what the change is, and are kept current with it, so the git history is informative without the diff.
A note addressed to reviewers (an alternative considered, an open choice) is made as a PR comment, not left as a comment in the code.
An `iff` lemma puts the more complex or composite side on the left and the simpler side on the right, so that it reads and rewrites as a simplification.
A deprecation, or a note that a declaration is discouraged or to be removed, points to a live replacement, never to nothing and never to another deprecated declaration.
Where the library provides notation for a notion (`[[a, b]]` for `uIcc`), statements use the notation rather than the underlying name.

A function-valued definition, field or local `have` puts its binders or pattern-matching equations in its header (`f x y := e`, `f | pat => e`, `have h (x) (hx : p x) : … := …`), not in a `fun` after `:=` or introduced afterwards with `intro`.
A wrapper type is a one-field structure, whose constructor and projection are the conversions, rather than a `def` synonym with hand-made equivalences.
A definition generalised to a weaker setting (semiring for ring) is the mathematically right notion there, not a transliteration that happens to typecheck.
A declaration body (statement and proof) contains no blank line.
An instance whose name matters — because an attribute (`@[simps]`, `@[to_dual]`, `@[to_additive]`) derives names from it or because it is referenced — is named explicitly rather than left anonymous.
A namespace whose members are used repeatedly in a section is opened (`open Foo in`) rather than written out at each use.
A definition is unfolded by naming it in `simp`, `rw` or `unfold`, not by a `show _ = _ from rfl` or a `change` that restates its body.
A statement about a filter (`∀ᶠ`, `Tendsto`) is used through the filter API rather than unpacked into explicit sets and membership.
When a structure is built from an existing structure that supplies several of its fields, those fields are inherited with `__ := existing` rather than copied one by one.
A proof line that packs several non-trivial mathematical moves into one dense expression is split into separate steps, even if longer.
A name component is written in its unambiguous form (`VonNeumann`, `finset_sum`) when the short form could refer to something else.
A definition analogous to an existing library function (a sum, a fold, a map) takes its arguments in the same shape and order as that function.
A bound variable that the body does not use is written as `_` (or cleared with `-` in `rintro`/`obtain`), not given a name.
A lemma that moves a cast through an operation or a literal is tagged `@[norm_cast]`.
A `simps` attribute is configured (`@[simps! apply]`) so that the generated lemma is stated at the level of application downstream uses need, not fully applied.
A definition obtained by reusing another across a definitional equality restates the fields whose types differ (`toFun`), so that generated lemmas mention the intended types.
A variable named after a Greek letter is written with the Unicode letter (`μ`, `φ`), not its transliteration (`mu`, `phi`).
A test of a tactic asserts the state it produces (`guard_target`, `guard_hyp`), not only that the tactic runs without error.
A type synonym introduced to carry instances different from the original type's is kept opaque to typeclass inference, not marked reducible for it.
Inside a tactic proof an instance hypothesis is introduced with `have`, not `haveI`; `haveI` is reserved for statements and term-mode where inlining is needed.
In a definition, the data it is built from is an explicit argument even when a hypothesis argument determines it, because a definition is applied to the data rather than to the proof.
A docstring that introduces a variable or a piece of notation says what the variable ranges over.
A definition or statement of the form `∀ x, x ∈ s → …` makes the bound variable strict-implicit (`∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → …`), so that it is inferred from the membership proof.
A name does not spell out hypotheses — instance hypotheses (`fully_faithful`, `preserves_mono`) or an `_of_h` suffix (`_of_isOpen`) — that are not needed to distinguish it from another declaration.
An instance needed in several proofs of a section is registered once as a `local instance` rather than obtained by a `have` in each proof.
A linter's complaint (a shake-flagged import, a flexible non-terminal `simp`) is fixed at its source rather than silenced by a `set_option linter.* false` or a `noshake.json` exception.
A purely stylistic change that the style guide does not prescribe is left to the author's discretion and is not imposed by a third party.
An attribute on a declaration tagged `to_additive` is passed through `to_additive (attr := …)` so that the additive version receives it too.
A definition takes a concrete bundled morphism type (`RingEquiv`) as its argument, not a `FooClass`-generic one; `FooClass` hypotheses are for lemmas.
A proof uses the most elementary tools that suffice, so that the result can be placed as early in the import hierarchy as possible.
A lemma's conclusion is stated in its simplest form (`1`, not `exp 0`), not in an expression that simplifies further.
A file does not pull in imports from a distant or heavier part of the library for a minor need; the dependency is avoided or the needed lemma stated in a lower file.
A new definition that is definitionally a known library object is connected to it by an explicit (possibly `rfl`) equivalence or lemma, so the connection is discoverable.
A structure field does not quantify over all types of a universe when a formulation over the carrier itself suffices.
A structure's axioms are chosen so that its morphisms are the natural maps; a laxer variant that makes maps awkward gets its own name (`Pre…`).
A small number of general lemmas are placed in the existing file where their subject lives (as `#find_home` suggests), not in a new file created for them.
When a lemma is generalised, its new hypothesis is a class that the original setting satisfies by an instance, so the special case still applies without extra work.
The general algebraic lemma is used rather than its type-specific copy (`zero_mul`, not `Nat.zero_mul`) when both apply.
A membership characterisation `mem_foo : x ∈ foo ↔ …` is named without an `_iff` suffix; the `↔` is implied by the `mem_` form.
A lemma about a type synonym is stated through the synonym's own API (its own `valuation`), not by applying the original structure across the definitional equality.
A definition written for kernel reduction or proof convenience that is slow to execute is paired with an efficient implementation via `@[csimp]`.

The dual of a lemma is obtained from the original — generated by `to_dual`/`to_additive`, or derived by applying the original at the order dual (`α := αᵒᵈ`) — rather than stated and proved again by hand.

A deprecated declaration whose replacement has a different signature (other explicit arguments or hypotheses) is kept with its original statement under `@[deprecated]`, not aliased to the replacement, so existing uses keep compiling.
A declaration's docstring points to closely related, overlapping or stronger declarations elsewhere in the library (`See also …`).
A notion made a class, which fixes one canonical instance per type, is also available as a plain structure when a type naturally carries several of them at once.

When a new simp lemma changes the simp normal form, existing lemmas stated in the old form are restated (or given a version) in the new form, rather than the simp lemma being excluded with `-lemma` at use sites.
A lemma with hypotheses that `simp` must discharge is tagged `@[simp]` only with justification that its side conditions are ones `simp` reliably proves.
A goal that a lighter, more targeted tactic (`simp`, `omega`, `lia`, `cutsat`, `positivity`, `fun_prop`) closes is closed by that tactic rather than by a general-purpose search (`grind`, `aesop`).
A PR description follows Mathlib's template and states only what reviewers need; boilerplate sections (test plan, implementation notes) are left out.
A name carries a prime only to distinguish a variant from an existing unprimed declaration; a prime with no unprimed counterpart is dropped.
A definition's docstring, or the module docstring introducing the notion, says what the object is (its defining formula or characterisation), not merely a restatement of its type.
Declarations are placed in the namespace where the library keeps the analogous results about the same objects (the class or structure they concern), not at the root or in an unrelated namespace.

A constructor or function that takes many data and proof arguments, directly or inside a long existential hypothesis, bundles them into a structure and takes one term (or `Nonempty`) of it, so that structure-instance syntax and code actions apply.
A new structure or definition is not introduced only to package the content of a single statement; that statement is written as a lemma (an iff with an existential) instead.
The two directions of an `iff` are taken with `.mp`/`.mpr`, not `.1`/`.2`.
A file's name and directory describe its actual content; a file whose content has drifted from its name is moved or renamed.
An eponym in prose and docstrings is spelled as the name is: the adjective capitalised (Noetherian, Artinian, Hausdorff), a name particle lowercase (von Neumann).
The most general version of a construction takes the plain name; a special case is the one that carries a distinguishing suffix.
Meta-code invokes another tactic through its `MetaM`/`TacticM` implementation function rather than by building syntax and calling `evalTactic`.
A PR does not add new uses of API that is being deprecated or refactored; it waits for, or builds on, the replacement.

A field of a specific, non-canonical instance is accessed as a projection of that instance term (`(inst).field x`), not through the class projection with the instance pinned (`C.field (self := inst) x`, `@C.field … inst x`).
A name uses the library's standard spelling or abbreviation for a word or symbol (`fun` for function, `hom`, `equiv`, `notMem` for `∉`), not a different one.
A test case carries a comment saying what behaviour it checks, so that later edits do not defeat its purpose.
A docstring that points to another file refers to it by its file name, in the form the library uses elsewhere.
The docstring of a `TFAE` or otherwise indexed statement lists the items with numbers matching their indices, not bullets.
A PR title follows the commit convention: a type prefix (`feat`, `chore`, `fix`) with the area in parentheses, then a concise description.
A tactic proof opens with `by` at the end of the `:=` line, not at the start of the next line.
Lemmas that a generator attribute produces — projection lemmas with `@[simps]`, the characterising iff of a structure or class with `@[mk_iff]` — are generated rather than written by hand.
Lemmas about the components of an applied function are named with the projection as a suffix (`f_apply_fst`), following the `simps` naming, not with the projection first (`fst_f`).
A local term that carries data (a `Fintype` instance, a function) is introduced with `let`, not `have`, so that its value is not forgotten.
Lemmas assume the weakest class that supplies exactly what they use; when the needed combination of existing classes has no name, a class for it is introduced.
A PR that replaces proofs by heavier automation (`grind`, `simp_all`) reports its measured effect on compile time.

When a cleanup removes the last violation of a layering or dependency rule, the corresponding linter (directory dependency, forbidden import) is strengthened to forbid it, so the cleanup cannot regress.

A term-mode body (a proof or a structure instance) follows `:=` on the statement line only when the whole declaration fits on one line; otherwise `:=` ends the statement and the body begins on the next line.
Rewriting or unfolding at default transparency (`erw`-style behaviour) is tracked as technical debt; new tooling or options that enable it are not added.
A goal that `rfl` closes only by unfolding definitions is instead proved by rewriting with the API lemmas stating those equalities, so the proof does not rely on definitional unfolding.
A definition that merely abbreviates a short expression in existing operations (`t + 1`) is not added; the expression is written directly.
A goal of the form `∀ᶠ x in l, p x` is proved with `filter_upwards [h₁, …] with x hx`, not by a manual `Eventually.mono`/`eventually_of_mem` application followed by `intro`.
A property needed only by some results (a size bound, non-degeneracy, coplanarity) is a hypothesis on those lemmas, not a field of a separate structure defined for the restricted case.

A function's non-obvious behaviour or presumed context (a mode it forces, an environment it assumes) is stated in its docstring, and reflected in its name where it matters, not only in an internal comment.
A tactic acts on the hypotheses it needs, named explicitly (`at h₁ h₂ ⊢`), not on the whole context with `at *`.
An instance that nothing refers to by name is left anonymous, taking the auto-generated name, rather than named by hand.

A tactic is chosen for the work it actually does: a `norm_num` or `simp` call whose only effect is rewriting with one lemma is written as `simp only [that lemma]` or `rw`, and a normaliser (`ring_nf`) that closes the goal is written as the closing form (`ring`).

Casts are normalised with the cast tactics (`push_cast`, `norm_cast`, `mod_cast`), not by listing cast lemmas (`Int.cast_add`, `Int.cast_neg`, `Nat.cast_ofNat`) in a `simp only` nor by a general `simp`/`simpa` whose only work is the casts.
A lemma that holds only under a restrictive hypothesis carries that hypothesis in its name (`_of_subsingleton`), so the name does not promise more than the statement.
A statement bundling two independently useful facts (an `IsGreatest`, a conjunction) is stated as one lemma per fact.
Notation that is standard in its area is declared `scoped` in the relevant namespace, so other files can open it, rather than `local` to one file.
An `example` does not live in a library file: a check of a tactic goes to the test suite, a fact worth keeping becomes a theorem, and the rest is removed.
An equation between composable morphisms in a category is tagged `@[reassoc]` (typically `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`) so it also applies inside longer compositions.
A declaration's name follows the pattern of its siblings and of the library's analogous declarations (same suffixes, same elisions), not a scheme of its own.
A multi-line comment not attached to a declaration is written as a `/- … -/` block, not a run of `--` lines and not `/-- … -/`, which is reserved for docstrings.
Declaration names and other code (variables, expressions) in comments and docstrings are enclosed in backticks so the documentation renders and links them.
A lemma's name states its conclusion first and its hypotheses after `_of_`, in that order.
A docstring or a TODO item says concretely what the declaration does or uses, or what remains to be done, not a vague gesture (`relevant information`, `some conditions`).
Declarations about one notion (a definition and its lemmas) are grouped together in a file, not scattered among unrelated sections.
A lemma's name matches the form of its statement: an iff carries `_iff`, a `_mono` lemma is the monotonicity implication; a statement of a different form takes the name of that form.
A private or auxiliary declaration is given a descriptive name following the naming convention, not a placeholder such as `aux`.
The closing delimiter of a structure instance or anonymous constructor (`}`, `⟩`) is placed at the end of the last field's line, not on a line of its own.
A cast between number types is written with the canonical coercion (`Nat.cast`, `(↑)`), not the type's own constructor or conversion function (`Int.ofNat`).
A type defined as a quotient exposes its own `lift`, `lift₂` and induction API, and downstream files use that API rather than raw `Quotient` operations on the underlying construction.
An instance named by hand takes the lowerCamelCase name of the class it provides (`categoryStruct`), without an unnecessary namespace prefix or the auto-generated `inst` spelling.
Paired one-line lemmas (a lemma and its symmetric or dual twin) are written on consecutive lines with no blank line between them, so the pair reads as a unit.

A definition that transports data along an equality of indices (`ZMod n` for equal `n`) uses the library's congruence equivalence for that type (`ringEquivCongr`), not `rw`, `▸` or `cast` on the term.
A landmark theorem added to the library is recorded in the documentation index (`docs/overview.md`, `docs/100.yaml`).
A lemma's conclusion is stated with a bare variable where possible, moving structure such as a complement into the hypothesis, so that the conclusion unifies with more goals.
An auxiliary definition with a short body and a single use is inlined at that use rather than declared as a separate `aux` definition.
A lemma that is useful as a simp lemma is kept rather than deprecated; `@[simp]` and `@[deprecated]` do not sit on the same declaration.
A declaration is deprecated in favour of another only when the replacement states the same result; a lemma whose content differs from the proposed replacement is kept.
A side hypothesis that a standard tactic discharges from context (`by lia`, `by simp`) is given as an auto-param (`:= by tac`) so that callers need not supply it.
A sum or product over a `Finset` is indexed by membership (`∑ x ∈ s, f x`), not by the coerced subtype (`∑ x : s, f x`).
A docstring is written in English prose (`homomorphism`, not `hom`; `a complete equipartite subgraph`, not the Lean expression for it), not in the abbreviations or code of declaration names.
A theorem's universally quantified variables and hypotheses are declared as binders before the colon, not as a `∀` or `→` in the conclusion.
A suggestion for an open PR is made on that PR (a review comment or a push to its branch), not by opening a second PR for the same change.
A lemma with a dual or mirror variant is named so that the name distinguishes the two (naming the direction of its hypothesis), even when only one of them is being added.
Meta-code that branches on a known set of syntax kinds fails explicitly on an unexpected kind rather than silently falling through to a default branch.
A structure whose elements are applied as functions registers a `FunLike` instance, with its coercion and `ext` lemmas derived from it, not a bare `CoeFun`.

A type or category variable is declared with the `*` binder (`Type*`, `Sort*`, `[Category* C]`), not fixed to a universe (`Type`) nor given an explicitly named universe (`Type u`) that nothing else needs, nor `[Category C]`.

A file-level explanation (what the file proves, its strategy, its references, its TODO list) is placed in the module docstring at the top of the file, not in a separate `/- -/` or `/-! -/` comment block.
A lemma about a type or function defined in core or Batteries (`List`, `Nat`) is upstreamed there rather than added to Mathlib, so that projects not depending on Mathlib benefit.
A better name or statement is adopted even when it requires deprecating the old one; the number of deprecations is not a cost to be minimised.
An open question or item left in the code is marked with the standard `TODO` tag, not an ad hoc marker (`XXX`, `FIXME`).

A case split is made with `obtain`/`rcases` on a library dichotomy lemma (`eq_zero_or_pos`, `eq_or_lt_of_le`) that yields a substitutable `rfl` and the useful strict form in each branch, not with `by_cases` on an equality.
A structure's axiom fields form a minimal independent set; a field that follows from the others is proved as a lemma, not required of every instance.
Of two lemmas that `simp` could apply to the same term (a dependent and a non-dependent form), `@[simp]` goes on the form goals commonly take, not on both or on the rarer one.
Notation is introduced for a notion only when it reads markedly better than the name; a notation that merely saves a few characters is not added.
A declaration with a universe level that its arguments do not determine is tagged `@[pp_with_univ]` so that the level is displayed.
A typeclass fact proved inline for a general situation (`have : Subsingleton …`, `let _ : Module.Free …`) is registered as a global instance rather than established at each use.
An instance that fixes one of several reasonable structures on a type (an order on matrices or on `ℂ`) is declared `scoped` in a namespace users open, not globally.
An inline (non-doc) comment writes mathematics in Unicode and backticks, not LaTeX, since it is read only in the source.
The import block is contiguous: no blank line separates `public import` lines from `import` lines.
A file or directory is named in the singular (`Polygon`, not `Polygons`).
When a new general lemma is added, existing code elsewhere in the library or Archive that proves its special cases by hand is refactored to use it.
A behaviour the library claims happens automatically (an instance inferred after an import) is checked by a test in the test suite.

A new function of a kind the library bundles (an arithmetic function, a homomorphism, a measure) is defined as a term of that bundled type rather than as a bare function, so that the bundled API applies to it.
A relation or predicate that serves only as the body of an instance (`≤`, `<`) is inlined into that instance rather than given its own named structure.
A file that sits below `Mathlib.Init` in the import hierarchy imports the header linter itself, so that its copyright header and module docstring remain checked.
A statement or instance header writes out the terms it refers to (`M ⧸ N`) rather than leaving them as `_` for the elaborator to fill, so that it reads without elaboration.
A tactic proof of one or two short steps is written inline after `by` on the `:=` line (`by ext; simp`), not spread over a multi-line block.
An equation relied on by a `rfl` simp lemma or an instance holds at reducible transparency; a construction whose basic equations hold only after unfolding is restructured so that they do.
An element of a quotient is introduced through its induction principle (`induction x using Quotient.inductionOn`), not destructured with `obtain ⟨x⟩`, which exposes the raw constructor.
The alternatives of a `cases`/`induction … with` or a `match` each stand on their own line, not packed onto one line.
Code written around a helper or API that does not yet exist carries a `TODO` naming the intended replacement, so the follow-up is recorded where it applies.
A code span in a docstring or comment is kept on one line, not broken across a line break.
A result is consumed in the shape the producing tactic (`choose`, `obtain`) gives it, not restated as an explicit `∃` only to be destructured again into an equivalent form.
An equation or iff lemma that `grind` should rewrite with is tagged `@[grind =]`.
The `## Tags` list of a module docstring holds search terms a reader would type (English names of the notion), not declaration names or near-duplicates of each other.
Two propositions or predicates are related by `↔` (stated pointwise), not by an equality of `Prop`s or of `Prop`-valued functions.
A statement about the elements of a set or subgroup quantifies over the ambient type with a membership hypothesis (`∀ γ ∈ Γ`, `s : Set G`), not over the coerced subtype (`∀ γ : Γ`, `Set Γ`).
The import block is sorted alphabetically.
The module docstring's `Main statements` list names only the file's principal results; routine or trivial lemmas are left out of it.
A docstring's text begins on the same line as the opening `/--`, not on the following line.

The structural skeleton of a proof (splitting a conjunction or iff, introducing variables) is given up front by one `refine ⟨fun x ↦ ?_, fun y ↦ ?_⟩`, not by successive `constructor` and `intro` steps.
A lemma establishing a function property (continuity, measurability, differentiability) for a construction or operation is tagged `@[fun_prop]` so that `fun_prop` can discharge it.
A `noncomputable` marker goes on the definitions that need it; `noncomputable section` is used only when most of a section's definitions are noncomputable.

A special-purpose piece of code solving one instance of a general problem is not added when a general solution is wanted; the general solution is designed instead of taking on code that will be replaced.
A lemma registered in a simp set is stated in the orientation in which the set rewrites, rather than stated backwards and registered with `←`.
A PR changes only what its purpose requires; an incidental rewrite of working code (a term step turned into a tactic step, a declaration moved) is left out.
Text explaining a declaration is written as its docstring (`/-- … -/`), not as a `--` comment above it.
A structure's data field has a plain type, with the property it must satisfy stated as a separate `Prop` field, rather than a subtype that packs the property into the data.
A definition that varies an existing library notion (a compactness variant) is phrased in the same form as that notion (through filters), with the other characterisations stated as lemmas.

A declaration is not given a short generic name in the root namespace (`E`) or in a generic namespace (`Derivative.deriv_num` for a fact about modular forms); it is placed in the namespace of its subject, made scoped notation, or given a longer specific name so that it does not clash with or suggest other uses.
A notion or lemma (a structure, a class, an intermediate definition, a factored-out lemma) is added only when something uses or will use it; one without a consumer is not introduced.
A proof that crosses an abstraction boundary makes the unfolding visible with an explicit `unfold` or `simp only [def]` step rather than letting a tactic see through the definition silently.
Declarations sharing a namespace prefix are placed inside a `namespace` block rather than each spelled with the prefix.
Declarations needing different typeclass assumptions are grouped in sections each declaring exactly its assumptions, not in one section with `omit` and `include` adjusting them per declaration.
A workaround for a defeq or elaboration problem is applied at the declaration where the problem originates, not at a downstream declaration where it surfaces.
A long proof is made followable: its structure is simplified, reusable parts are split into lemmas, and the remaining non-obvious steps carry explanatory comments.
A non-terminal `simp` whose result feeds one closing step is restructured so that the `simp` is terminal (`simpa using`), rather than squeezed to `simp only`.
A PR of LLM-generated code whose author does not understand it well enough to improve it through review is closed rather than reviewed.

A result about a structure obtained from a particular constructor is stated for any instance satisfying the defining condition (an iff in terms of the data), not with a `letI` pinning that construction.
Several equivalent characterisations of one property are collected in a `List.TFAE` statement, with the individual iffs derived from it.
A PR that depends on another open PR declares the dependency in its description with the `depends on` syntax, so that the dependency label is applied automatically.
An expression for a mathematical object that recurs across an area (the all-ones matrix) is given its own definition with API rather than written out at each use.

A file's copyright header names the year and authors of the contribution that created its content: the current year and author for new material, the original authors and year for content split out of another file.
In a docstring, a bullet list is separated from the surrounding paragraphs by a blank line.

A statement or definition is not generalised (semilinear maps for linear maps, an extra parameter, a weaker algebraic assumption that loses operations users rely on) beyond what a use needs when the generality complicates it; unused generality is dropped.

A variable bound in a statement, a term in it, or a `have` in a proof whose type is not evident from its use is given an explicit type ascription rather than left to inference or a bare coercion arrow.
A declaration important enough to be a `theorem` rather than a `lemma` carries a docstring; one not worth documenting is a `lemma`.
Among equivalent formulations of a definition, the one under which its basic characterising lemma (membership, application) holds by `rfl` is chosen.
A docstring is attached to the declaration it describes; text describing another declaration or the overall design is moved to that declaration or to the module docstring.
Infrastructure that runs on every declaration by default (a linter, an analysis framework) has its idle cost measured before it is enabled.
A negation or disequality goal (`a ≠ b`, `¬ p`) is proved by introducing its hypothesis (`intro h`, `rintro rfl`), not by `by_contra`.
An equation obtained by destructuring an existential or a hypothesis is substituted at once with the `rfl` pattern (`obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩`), not named and rewritten with afterwards.
Variables of the same type and binder kind are declared in one binder group (`{A B C : Type*}`), not split across several groups.
Deprecated declarations that no longer fit the file they were in are moved to a file under `Mathlib/Deprecated/`, not kept in place or deleted.
A lemma's docstring is written only when it adds to the statement (its meaning, its role); a docstring that repeats the statement verbatim is omitted.
A reducible definition is declared with `abbrev`, not with `@[reducible] def`.
Of several equivalent formulations of a notion, the one most convenient in applications is the definition and the others are proved as characterisation lemmas.
A non-obvious mathematical assertion in a docstring or comment is supported by a citation.
A multi-line tactic proof is not nested inside an anonymous constructor or argument list (`⟨a, by …⟩`); the term is given with `refine` and `?_` and the proof follows as its own goal.

A property defined in `At`/`On` forms also has its unqualified global form (`Meromorphic` beside `MeromorphicOn`, as `Continuous` beside `ContinuousOn`), so that statements need not quantify over `univ`.
Lemmas describing how a map interacts with a lattice or algebraic structure cover the distinguished elements (`⊥`, `⊤`, `0`, `1`) as well as the binary operations (`⊔`, `⊓`, `+`, `*`).
A lemma stating a generally useful fact about a definition is public API, not `private`; `private` is reserved for implementation details that only build the public API.

A module docstring section is kept only when it tells the reader something specific to the file; a boilerplate section copied from sibling files (a notation list of the standard variable names) is omitted.
A new notion that refines or parallels an existing one (a star projection beside an idempotent) is given the analogues of the existing notion's API lemmas.
A `calc` chain starts from the goal as stated; a preliminary normalisation (`simp only`, unfolding) is performed as a step before the `calc`, not as its first link.
In a `module` file whose API is curated declaration by declaration, each declaration that downstream files must see — an instance, a definition used in public statements — is marked `public`.

When a hypothesis or conclusion is phrased in a spelling the library has little API for (`a ∈ l.dropLast`) while an equivalent spelling is well supported (`a ≠ l.getLast _`), a lemma connecting the two spellings is provided, or the well-supported spelling is used.

A name supplied to a generator attribute (`to_additive`, `to_fun`, `to_dual`) is given only when it differs from the name the attribute would generate on its own; a name equal to the generated one is omitted.
A notation is declared at a precedence (`:max` for a bracketed or postfix form) that lets its applications stand as function arguments without parentheses.

When standard automation (`fun_prop`, `simp`, `positivity`) fails on a goal of a form it is meant to handle, the gap is closed — the missing lemma tagged, or the statement rephrased in the form it handles — rather than the goal discharged by hand at the use site.
`Algebra` and `IsScalarTower` instances arising from ring homomorphisms are introduced with `algebraize`, not by a hand-written `letI` for each.
A `Prop`-valued class or predicate on a type is named with the `Is` prefix (`IsPolynormableSpace`), the bare noun being reserved for data-carrying classes.
A class or structure all of whose fields are proofs is declared `: Prop`.

A structure-instance literal spanning several lines places its braces consistently: `{` on the first field's line and `}` at the end of the last, or each brace on its own line; not `{` trailing the `:=` line with `}` closing the last field.
A lemma that most `simp` calls in a file need but that is unsuitable as a global simp lemma is registered once with `attribute [local simp]` at the top of the file, not supplied to each call.
A proof by contradiction opens with `by_contra!`, which also pushes the negation inward, not with a rewrite to a negated form (`← not_…_iff`) followed by `intro`.
A hypothesis is named after the variable it constrains (`hc : c ≠ 0`), not with a name copied from a sibling lemma's hypothesis about a different variable.
AI-generated code is cleaned up by the author before it is submitted for review: narrative comments removed, convoluted arguments simplified, linter-flagged patterns (non-terminal `simp`) fixed.
An improvement to a tactic's behaviour that is wanted in every use becomes its default rather than a `!` variant; a variant is added only when the old behaviour remains needed.
A docstring writes a short expression in Unicode and backticks (`T : ℕ → ℝ`, `aᵢ`) wherever they can express it, reserving LaTeX for display formulas Unicode cannot render.
A hypothesis of the form `∃ e, P e ∧ Q e` is taken as separate arguments (`e`, `he : P e`, `hx : Q e`), since callers hold the witness, rather than as one existential.

A note on an instance that disagrees with an existing instance on the same type states precisely how the two relate — a genuine diamond, or mathematically distinct notions built from different data — rather than saying vaguely that they conflict.
A `conv` block that replaces part of the goal by an equal term is written instead as a `suffices` or `have` stating that equality, followed by a rewrite.

When two hypotheses are equivalent in a lemma's setting (second-countable and Lindelöf for metric spaces; bounded and locally bounded variation on a segment), the lemma assumes the one the library conventionally uses there, the simpler or more common notion.
A declaration's explicit arguments put the principal object (the one in whose namespace it lives) before the auxiliary data, so that it reads naturally with dot notation.
An existence theorem whose witness is a canonical construction is given as a named definition of the witness with lemmas stating its properties; the existential statement is derived as a corollary.
A section or namespace that groups the material about one declaration is named after that declaration, with the declaration's own spelling and casing.
A side condition of a rewrite or application that a tactic can discharge is left as the side goal `rw`/`apply` creates and closed by that tactic, not constructed by hand and passed as an argument.
A structure that adds conditions to an existing bundled structure is declared with `extends` rather than with a field holding a term of that structure.

In category theory, the universes of a category's objects and morphisms are declared as named universe variables (`universe v u`, `Category.{v} C`), not left as universe-level metavariables through `Type*` and `[Category C]`, which hinder automation and performance.

A theorem whose statement is an `iff` or a structure of proofs is proved with `constructor`, an anonymous constructor or `refine`, not with `where`-field syntax, which makes a theorem read like a definition.
Meta-code that tests whether two expressions coincide uses a (reducible) definitional-equality check, not syntactic equality `==`.
A function given pointwise by an algebraic operation or constant (`fun n ↦ Y n - X n`, `fun _ ↦ 1`) is written through the pointwise instance on functions (`Y - X`, `1`), not as a lambda.
A type-specific lemma is deprecated in favour of its general algebraic version only when the typeclass search the general version triggers at each use is acceptable.
A private or auxiliary technical declaration carries a docstring saying why it exists, so that a reader need not hunt for its purpose.
A finiteness fact is registered as a `Finite` instance; a noncomputable `Fintype` instance is not declared when `Finite` serves.
A `simp` whose resulting goal is passed to a following tactic (a non-terminal `simp`) is squeezed to `simp only [...]` or restructured so that it is terminal; it is not left as a flexible `simp`.
A docstring that is a noun phrase rather than a complete sentence does not end with a full stop.
A trace or diagnostic message is a neutral, descriptive statement of what was found or done, not colloquial or exclamatory text.
A symmetry rewrite (`iff_comm`, `eq_comm`) whose only purpose is to match the goal's orientation is avoided by arranging the proof's parts or the lemma's arguments in the goal's order.
A function given as a chain of compositions (`f ∘ g ∘ h`) in a statement is written as an explicit lambda (`fun x ↦ f (g (h x))`) when that reads more clearly.
A PR whose design or content was discussed on Zulip links that discussion in its description.

A class or structure that refers to a type carrying its own instances (a category, a preadditive structure) takes that type and its instances as parameters rather than bundling them as fields, so that their structure is syntactic and no definitional unfolding is forced.
